msg.content: Who was the head of government in the countries that won each of the last 5 FIFA World Cups at the time of their victories?
Who was the head of government in the countries that won each of the last 5 FIFA World Cups at the time of their victories?

content.content:
We need to answer: For each of last 5 FIFA World Cups, who was the head of government (likely the prime minister or president) of the country that won it, at the time of their victory. Let's list last 5 World Cups: 2022 Qatar, 2018 Russia, 2014 Brazil, 2010 South Africa, 2006 Germany. Winners: Argentina (2022), France (2018), Germany (2014), Spain (2010), Italy (2006). Identify head of government of each country at that time.

Argentina 2022: President was Alberto Fernández (since Dec 10 2019). Head of government is the President. So Alberto Fernández.

France 2018: President was Emmanuel Macron (since May 14 2017). So Emmanuel Macron.

Germany 2014: Chancellor was Angela Merkel (since 2005, until 2021). So Angela Merkel.

Spain 2010: Prime Minister was José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero (2004-2011). So José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero.

Italy 2006: Prime Minister was Silvio Berlusconi (second term 2001-2006, actually until May 2006; he was PM until May 22 2006, when he was succeeded by Romano Prodi). The World Cup final was on July 9, 2006, after Berlusconi had left office? Wait, let's recall: In 2006, Berlusconi resigned after his conviction. He was replaced by Romano Prodi, who became PM on May 22, 2006, before the World Cup. So head of government at time of victory (July 9, 2006) was Romano Prodi. But Prodi's term was from 22 May 2006 to 8 May 2008. So yes, head of government was Prime Minister Romano Prodi.

Thus answer: 2022 Argentina – President Alberto Fernández; 2018 France – President Emmanuel Macron; 2014 Germany – Chancellor Angela Merkel; 2010 Spain – Prime Minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero; 2006 Italy – Prime Minister Romano Prodi.

Need to verify each date: Argentina 2022 final July 18 2022. President Alberto Fernández. Yes.

France 2018 final July 15 2018. President Emmanuel Macron. Yes.

Germany 2014 final July 13 2014. Chancellor Angela Merkel. Yes.

Spain 2010 final July 11 2010. Prime Minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero. Yes.

Italy 2006 final July 9 2006. Prime Minister Romano Prodi. Yes.

Thus output accordingly. Provide a table or list. Also note that head of government refers to President in some countries, Prime Minister in others. Provide context.

content:
**Head of Government (at the time of the World‑Cup final)**  
| World Cup | Winning country | Date of final | Head of government (title) | Name |
|-----------|-----------------|--------------|---------------------------|------|
| 2022 | Argentina | 18 Jul 2022 | President | **Alberto Fernández** |
| 2018 | France | 15 Jul 2018 | President | **Emmanuel Macron** |
| 2014 | Germany | 13 Jul 2014 | Chancellor | **Angela Merkel** |
| 2010 | Spain | 11 Jul 2010 | Prime Minister | **José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero** |
| 2006 | Italy | 9 Jul 2006 | Prime Minister | **Romano Prodi** |

> *Note:* In Argentina, France, and Germany the head of state also serves as the head of government (President / Chancellor). In Spain and Italy, the role is that of the Prime Minister. All listed officials held their positions at the time the respective World Cup final was played.
